pdf_title: Diffusion GAN-Based Oversampling for Imbalanced Tabular Data
srcdet: Table I groups datasets by source citation: [45] (UCI) supplies satimage, students_dropout, default, Dry_Beans, bank, nursery, abalone_15, abalone_6, polish_bankruptcy, avila, page-blocks, firewall (12); [48] (Python package imbalanced-learn) supplies optical_digits, satimage_4, pen_digits, sick_euthyroid, isolet, thyroid_sick, coil_2000, wine_quality, letter_img, abalone_19 (10).
imbalance_creation: Table I column '# T' gives the selected target class used as minority for binary tasks: 'minority' for most datasets; abalone_15 target '>=15', abalone_6 target '<=6' (UCI); imbalanced-learn datasets with targets 8 (optical_digits), 4 (satimage_4), 5 (pen_digits), A,B (isolet), <=4 (wine_quality), Z (letter_img), 19 (abalone_19). No undersampling or noise injection described. Multi-class datasets used with their class structure.
split_protocol: Stratified 5-fold cross-validation, repeated with ten random seeds for each resampling method; average performance reported
ir_definition: IR = Nmaj/Nmin, where Nmaj and Nmin are the number of majority and minority class instances; for multi-class datasets, the ratio between the number of instances in the class with the most and those with the fewest instances

evidence.quote: we employed 22 real-world tabular datasets to evaluate the performance of our model. These datasets comprise 15 binary classification datasets and seven multi-classification datasets.
All the datasets used in our experiments are publicly available, sourced from repositories including UCI [45] and the Python package imbalanced-learn [48].

Essential details for these datasets, including the selected target class (# T) as of minority class for binary classification, data size (# S), feature length (# F), the number of classes (# C), and the class imbalance ratio (IR), are summarized in Table I.
TABLE I DESCIPTION OF THE DATASETS Source Data Name # T # S # F # C IR

where Nmaj and Nmin represent the number of majority and minority class instances, respectively. For multi-class datasets, IR is the ratio between the number of instances in the class with the most and those with the fewest instances.
For each dataset, we employ a stratified 5-fold cross-validation approach, randomly dividing the dataset into five folds.

Resampling methods are then applied to balance the imbalance ratio within the training set. Subsequently, classification models are trained on the transformed training set and evaluated on the test data.
We repeat this procedure with ten random seeds for each resampling method and report their average performance.
Our code has been made publicly available at https://github.com/MLneuers/DGOT.
The DGOT achieves the best performance on 14 out of 22 datasets concerning accuracy, 18 out of 22 for F1-score, and 12 out of 22 for MCC.
